title: Engine Fire Handle Position Indication Disagreement — Fault Isolation
abstract: Fault isolation for a disagreement between the engine fire handle position and its reported state, covering microswitch adjustment after the detent modification and the guard interference case.

sections.purpose: Fault isolation for a reported disagreement between the physical position of an engine fire handle and the state reported by the microswitch, with the aircraft on the ground.
sections.fault_description: The reported case is a handle that is visibly stowed but reports pulled, or a handle that is pulled and does not report. On aircraft converted to the detent standard the microswitch actuation point moves by 4 mm, and a switch left at the pre-conversion adjustment gives exactly this disagreement. The second cause is the hinged guard: a guard that has not been assembled correctly can hold the handle a millimetre out of the stowed position, which is enough to make the switch and is not obvious to look at. The order of the checks below follows the design assessment; no in-service case has been recorded against the converted standard at the date of this issue.
sections.isolation_procedure: 1. Isolate the fire extinguishing bottles before any handle is moved. 2. Establish the handle standard fitted from the configuration record. 3. Examine the guard on the affected handle for correct assembly and confirm the handle sits fully stowed with the guard closed. 4. Where the handle is held out of the stowed position by the guard, correct the guard assembly and re-check; this is the cause in roughly a third of reports on converted aircraft. 5. Where the handle is fully stowed, check the microswitch actuation point against the value for the standard fitted. 6. Where the actuation point is at the pre-conversion value on a converted aircraft, adjust it and re-check. 7. Do the break-out force check to confirm the detent is functioning, because a weak detent lets the handle rest short of stowed. 8. Where all three are excluded, the microswitch itself has failed and the handle mechanism must be removed.
sections.dispatch_note: Dispatch with a fire handle position indication disagreement is not permitted. The handle is the crew's means of shutting down and isolating the engine, and an indication that cannot be trusted removes that assurance. The aircraft must not be released until the disagreement is resolved and the functional test has passed on all four handles.

possible_causes.cause: Microswitch left at the pre-conversion actuation point
Hinged guard holding the handle out of the stowed position
Weak detent letting the handle rest short of stowed

dispatch.dispatch_condition: No dispatch with a fire handle position indication disagreement
